ops-bot: :warning: apac-usw link between region-usw2 and apac-sin showing intermittent packet loss (0.3%-1.2%) impacting hedged cross-region calls

mina: noticed increased hedged latencies. looks like periodic microbursts from a handful of tenants with large embedding streams

tom: are those tenants on shared egress pools or dedicated?
mina: shared egress pool. traffic pattern is many small parallel embedding requests -> long-lived TCP flows that bulk transfer KV snapshots

viv: options: 1) migrate heavy embedding tenants to dedicated egress lanes 2) enable TCP pacing on host side 3) fall back to local embeddings model (smaller) when cross-region calls degrade

tom: prefer 2 + 3 for quick fix. pacing reduces burstiness without carving capacity. fallback reduces cross-region load.

mina: tcp pacing config (host): `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_congestion_control=cubic; sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1; tc qdisc add dev eth0 tbf rate 100mbit burst 32k latency 50ms` (per-tenant class)

viv: will add routing rule: `if link_loss>0.5% && call_type==embeddings -> prefer:local-small-embed else:hedge-crossregion`

ops-bot: Maintenance window for inter-region network at 2026-03-20T22:00:00Z. avoid manual reconfigs during that hour

mina: who can roll the tcp pacing? I can schedule for off-peak in 10m.

tom: I'll monitor. if p99 hedged latency >1s after 10m we escalate to neteng.

viv: rolling now. will post results in 15m.

ops-bot: tcp pacing applied to classes tenant-x,tenant-y at 2026-03-20T20:11:00Z by viv

mina: initial 10m: link loss down to 0.15%, hedged p95 dropped from 820ms to 310ms. good signal

tom: keep an eye for host-level retries. pacing can increase completion time for individual huge transfers but reduces spikes

viv: routing rule applied. fallback local embed now used for 17% of embedding calls. overall cross-region bandwidth down 22%

mina: if stable for 24h we can propose a permanent lane for heavy embedding tenants in apac

viv: filing a ticket for cost delta and next steps if they want permanent carveout.
